title: Logical Flaw in curl_url_set Leads to Inconsistent Query Parameter Encoding
excerpt:
Hello curl security team,

First, thank you for your incredible work on maintaining such a critical and robust piece of software. We have been conducting a deep-dive source code audit of libcurl and believe we have identified a subtle logical flaw in the curl_url_set API that has security implications.

## Summary

The curl_url_set() function in lib/urlapi.c exhibits inconsistent URL encoding behavior for the CURLUPART_QUERY part. The logic that determines whether to percent-encode the = character is incorrectly tied to the CURLU_APPENDQUERY flag, rather than being based purely on the CURLU_URLENCODE flag.

This causes the exact same input string to be encoded in two different ways depending on whether the query is being replaced or appended, which can lead to HTTP Parameter Pollution (HPP) vulnerabilities in applications that rely on libcurl.

## Affected Code

lib/urlapi.c, function curl_url_set(), specifically:

1. Line ~1832: equalsencode = appendquery;

   * This logic incorrectly bases the equalsencode flag on whether an append operation is happening.

2. Line ~1868: ((*i == '=') && equalsencode)

   * This line later uses equalsencode to decide whether to skip encoding the = character.

Because equalsencode is only true during an append operation, a replace operation (even with CURLU_URLENCODE) will result in equalsencode being false, causing it to incorrectly encode the = character.

## Proof of Concept (PoC)

In the interest of full transparency, an AI assistant was utilized to help write and refine the C code for the accompanying Proof of Concept.

To confirm this inconsistent behavior, we wrote the following C program. It tests the exact same input string ("a=b&c=d") under three different scenarios using the curl_url_set API.

key_reasons: The divergent '=' encoding is intentional: CURLU_APPENDQUERY is documented as 'append a form style part' (include/curl/urlapi.h:95), meaning the input is a single key=value pair where the first '=' is a delimiter. The replace path treats the input as a raw string. This is a documented semantic difference, not a bug.

The claimed HTTP Parameter Pollution (HPP) does not occur because all other special characters (:, /, &, etc.) are still percent-encoded in both modes (lib/urlapi.c:1866-1881). The attack scenario's example 'callback=http://attacker.com' would have ':' and '/' encoded to '%3A' and '%2F' even in append mode.

The project's 'API misuse' policy applies: the report describes a behavior difference between two documented API modes, not a flaw that gives an attacker capabilities they did not already have. Applications choose the mode appropriate to their input format.
reply: Thank you for the detailed report and PoC. The code shows the different '=' handling is intentional: CURLU_APPENDQUERY means 'append a form-style key=value part' (see include/curl/urlapi.h:95), so the first '=' is a delimiter and is preserved; the replace path treats the input as a raw string. This semantic difference is documented by the flag's purpose. Crucially, all other special characters (:, /, &, etc.) are still percent-encoded in both modes (lib/urlapi.c:1866-1881), so the described HPP vector (injecting unencoded ':' or '/') does not occur. The PoC confirms the behavioral difference, but it is a documented API distinction, not a security flaw. We consider this 'API misuse' per our policy — the application must choose the mode matching its input format.
